# [EPIC] Backlog audit: every artifact Scrum-shaped, true to the code, proven by tests

## Epic
Bring every issue on this board to one standard:

1. It matches its issue template.
2. It is written to the repo writing standard.
3. Its claims match the code as it is now.
4. Every acceptance criterion names a test or command that proves it.

Scope: the 193 issues that predate this epic. 12 epics, 38 stories, 130
tasks, 13 bugs.

Structure. One Story per epic under audit: #1, #10, #15, #22, #30, #35,
#39, #74, #76, #121, #136, #195. Under each, one Task per story under that
epic, and that Task's acceptance criteria name every task under that story
individually. Nothing is audited as a group, so nothing is skipped.

Three more Stories cover what hangs off no epic:

- #312, the 13 bugs, which sit outside the Epic to Story to Task hierarchy.
- #316, the 10 tasks that belong to no story.
- #311, the templates and the audit tooling. It stays open for the life of
  this epic, so a template or skill change found mid-audit lands there.

## Business Value
Closing an issue without proof removes it from review, so nobody re-checks
it. If each criterion names a test, CI fails when the behaviour breaks.
Without a test, the break is not detected.

## Product Goal alignment
Indirect. This epic ships no product feature. The backlog is where features
are specified and accepted, so incorrect issues propagate into what gets
built from them.

## Notes
The four gates (Shape, Voice, Truth, Proof) and the writing standard are in
`.claude/skills/audit-artifacts/`. `infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py`
checks the mechanical rules over one subtree or the whole board.

The 12 epic Stories plus #312 and #316 cover 199 of the 261 issues. The
other 62 are this epic and the audit issues opened under it. No Story
audits those; `audit-check.py --all` is what holds them to the standard.
